subject: Planned: EU-South rolling firmware & driver hotpatch (KV-cache preserve / exclusion request)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya@acmeanalytics.com>, platform-ops@acmeanalytics.com
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-01T08:14:00Z
Subject: Planned: EU-South rolling firmware & driver hotpatch (KV-cache preserve / exclusion request)

Hi Maya / Acme platform team,

Heads-up: we are scheduling a targeted maintenance window in the EU-South region to roll out a GPU firmware and kernel-driver hotpatch that resolves a rare eviction/latency regression we've seen at high token-concurrency. The goal of this run is to deploy a driver micro-patch and a small firmware update with an explicit KV-cache preservation flow to minimize cold-starts for streaming workloads.

Window (planned):
- Start: 2027-05-04 23:00 UTC
- End: 2027-05-05 03:30 UTC
- Rolling approach: sequential rack-by-rack restarts, ~10-15 min per host for driver swap + health checks, with automated KV-cache warmup for pinned pods. Total region duration ~4.5 hours.

What to expect:
- Impact: best-effort to keep inferences online; short spikes in P95 latency (up to ~300ms) for affected hosts during switchover. No mass evictions expected thanks to the KV-cache preservation flow, but there will be brief placement/connection handoffs.
- Affected surfaces: inference endpoints in eu-south (both hosted and Dedicated pools in the region). Control plane and management API remain available.
- Mitigations: automatic prefix/KV-cache preservation, graceful draining of long-lived sessions, and staged traffic shifting to warm hosts. We will monitor QPS and step back on any SLO regressions.

Recommended customer actions (optional but helpful):
- If you have nightly/batch jobs that start within the window, consider shifting them outside the window or add a short buffer to retry logic.
- For critical pools, you can request an exclusion (see below) so we patch those nodes in a separate, mutually-agreed maintenance window.

Attachments: eu-south-hotpatch-playbook.pdf (operator runbook), kvcache-preserve-checklist.txt, scheduled-window-ics.ics
Links: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/shared/eu-south-hotpatch-schedule, JIRA DRIVER-1293

Please reply with any constraints or an explicit exclusion request by 2027-05-02 16:00 UTC so we can finalize the schedule. If we don't hear back, we'll proceed with the window above.

Contact: me (neha.kapoor@redwood.ai) and Jordan (jordan.blake@redwood.ai) — we will run the customer comms and live runbook.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Manager, Site Reliability
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment stubs:
- eu-south-hotpatch-playbook.pdf (25 pages)
- kvcache-preserve-checklist.txt (script + checklist)
- scheduled-window-ics.ics (calendar invite)

From: Maya Singh <maya@acmeanalytics.com>

Date: 2027-05-01T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Planned: EU-South rolling firmware & driver hotpatch (KV-cache preserve / exclusion request)

Thanks for the heads-up, Neha — and for the detailed runbook. A couple of notes from our side: 

1) We have heavy nightly batch extract jobs that begin at 01:00 UTC on 2027-05-05 for the eu-south data pipelines. If possible, can we avoid the 00:00-02:00 UTC slice?
2) Our acme-prod-1 resource pool runs low-latency production traffic; can we request an exclusion for that pool and have it scheduled in a separate maintenance window next week?

If exclusion is possible, we'll coordinate a convenient secondary window. Otherwise we can shift our batch pipelines, but prefer not to.

Cheers,
Maya Singh
Platform Operations Manager
Acme Analytics

Neha / team,

Thanks — quick internal coord notes:
- We can offer an exclusion for acme-prod-1 by marking that tenant's node-labels as do-not-drain and scheduling a targeted patch next week (secondary window). That will require a manual gating step in the runbook and an ops engineer on-call to execute verification.
- Regarding the 00:00-02:00 UTC slice: we can shift the active patching to start 01:00 UTC instead of 23:00, and then extend into the early morning so we avoid the midnight batch overlap; this shifts the region-wide completion later (~06:30 UTC), but reduces risk for batch workloads.
- KV-cache preservation flow: Soojin will enable the warmup hooks and do a dry-run on the canary rack 48 hours prior. Vivek, please confirm we have sufficient spare warm hosts in eu-south to absorb the traffic spike if a host takes longer than expected.

Sooj, Vivek: can you confirm availability for the runbook dry-run and the on-call window?

Jordan
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

Hi Maya — thanks for the quick reply.

We can accommodate both asks with the following plan:
- Exclude: acme-prod-1 will be excluded from the main rolling window and scheduled for a secondary, mutually-agreed maintenance slot next week. We will add a manual verification gate for that pool and notify you of the slot by Friday.
- Adjusted window (for remainder of region): 2027-05-04 01:00 UTC -> 2027-05-05 06:30 UTC (extended end to allow later start)
  - This moves the high-risk slice away from your 01:00 nightly batch start and staggers canary->bulk phases later into the morning.
- Dry-run: Soojin will run the canary dry-run on 2027-05-03 08:00 UTC and share telemetry.

Action requested: please confirm Go / No-Go on the adjusted window and the exclusion by 2027-05-02 16:00 UTC so we can publish the final calendar invites and update the playbook.

We will also:
- Provide an internal runbook watch channel (join link included in attached ICS)
- Hold a 30-min pre-run brief with your ops team 1 hour before the start

Thanks — we will treat acme-prod-1 as excluded until the secondary slot is scheduled.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Manager, Site Reliability
Redwood Inference
